# ErikrafT Drop™

> ErikrafT Drop™ is an open-source, peer-to-peer file and text transfer application for moving content between devices without requiring an account.

## Overview

ErikrafT Drop™ provides browser-based device-to-device sharing with a focus on direct peer-to-peer communication, privacy, cross-platform access, and progressive web application support.

Canonical web application: https://drop.erikraft.com/

Current source version: **10.1.7**. Latest published web/desktop release: **10.1.6**.

Official source repository: https://github.com/erikraft/Drop

Related Android application: https://github.com/erikraft/Drop-Android

## Core capabilities

- Transfer files between connected devices.
- Send and receive text.
- Share images, videos, PDFs, documents and other supported files.
- Establish peer-to-peer connections using WebRTC.
- Pair devices for recurring transfers.
- Use public rooms for room-based connections.
- Use QR Code scanning and animated QR Code transfer workflows.
- Install the web application as a PWA where supported.
- Use supported Web Share Target and browser file-handler integrations.
- Use WebTorrent-based transfer functionality where supported.
- Configure Tor connectivity where supported.
- Use the desktop application on supported Windows and Linux environments.
- Use the separate Android application and its supported distribution channels.

## Transfer architecture

The web application uses WebRTC for peer-to-peer communication between participating devices. Server-side components provide application services such as connection/signaling coordination; ErikrafT Drop™ should not be described as a permanent cloud file-storage service.

Supported connection and transfer paths include WebRTC, the application's network/WebSocket infrastructure, animated QR workflows, public rooms, WebTorrent and Tor-related configuration. Availability depends on the browser, operating system, network environment, permissions and current build.

## Privacy and security

- No account is required for the basic transfer experience.
- Files are not intended to be stored permanently in a central cloud drive.
- WebRTC provides encrypted transport for compatible peer connections.
- The project is open source.
- Local browser/device storage may be used for application state such as pairing information.
- Network topology, signaling, browser behavior and optional transfer modes can affect how a transfer is established.

Privacy and security behavior should be understood from the current implementation, browser security model, network configuration and published policies.

## Smart Media, Metadata and Spin View

Recent versions include received-media tooling for supported images and videos:

- Inspect metadata from received media.
- Identify supported media and metadata information.
- Remove metadata from processed copies.
- Keep the original received file separate from processed copies.
- Prepare supported media for Spin View workflows.
- Preview supported media in the application's visual tools.

Metadata processing is intended to occur locally. The project should not be described as uploading EXIF, GPS, XMP, IPTC, media thumbnails, hashes, filenames or other private media metadata to a third-party analytics service.

Compatibility depends on the input format and current browser/application capabilities. Preparing media does not guarantee compatibility with every external service, social network, application or device.

## User-facing features

The current application includes or integrates functionality for file transfer, text transfer, device pairing, public rooms, QR scanning, animated QR transfer, notifications, PWA installation, theme selection, localization, Web Share Target, browser file handlers, WebTorrent transfer, Tor configuration, received-media metadata processing, Smart Media/Spin View workflows, Chat/WebChat, Page Agent-related browser features and iSearch CLI integration.

Some features are optional, experimental, platform-specific or dependent on browser APIs.

## Platforms

### Web

https://drop.erikraft.com/

The web application targets modern browsers with JavaScript and the required WebRTC capabilities. It can be installed as a PWA where supported.

### Desktop

The repository contains Electron desktop packaging for supported desktop environments.

- Releases: https://github.com/erikraft/Drop/releases
- Latest release: https://github.com/erikraft/Drop/releases/latest

Current web/desktop source version: **10.1.7**. Latest published release: **10.1.6**.

### Android

Android is maintained as a separate project with its own release lifecycle:

- Repository: https://github.com/erikraft/Drop-Android
- Releases: https://github.com/erikraft/Drop-Android/releases
- Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.erikraft.drop
- F-Droid: https://f-droid.org/en/packages/com.erikraft.drop/
- APKPure: https://apkpure.com/p/com.erikraft.drop

Do not assume Android release versions are identical to the web/desktop version.

## Project identity

Use the official product name **ErikrafT Drop™**.

### Alternate names

The following spelling variants may refer to the same product when users make informal or typographical variations: **ErikrafT Drop**, **ErikrafTDrop**, **Erik Craft Drop**, **ErikcrafT Drop**, and **EricrafT Drop**. The canonical product name remains **ErikrafT Drop™**.

Relevant terms: ErikrafT Drop, file transfer, file sharing, peer-to-peer file transfer, P2P, WebRTC, device-to-device transfer, text transfer, QR Code transfer, animated QR Code, public rooms, device pairing, PWA, WebTorrent, Tor, Smart Media, metadata, Spin View, Android file transfer, open-source file sharing.
